errors.problem: سَيَخْرُجُ is 3rd person masculine singular; 'they' is only true in one verb-first sentence with a plural subject
errors.fix: (he) will go out, will leave

errors.problem: سَيَأْتِي is singular (he/it will come); 'they' is a one-sentence reading
errors.fix: and (he, it) will come

errors.problem: the unvocalised key covers ظُهْرًا 'at noon' (very common after clock times: الثانية عشرة ظهرًا) as well as ظَهْرًا 'a back (object form)'; the gloss gives only the rarer reading, with no object-form note
errors.fix: at noon (ẕuhran); a back (ẕahran, object form)

errors.problem: the key covers عَبْرَ 'across, through, via' (a very common preposition) and عَبَرَ 'he crossed' as well as the imperative عَبِّرْ; the imperative is the least common reading
errors.fix: across, through, via (ʿabra); (he) crossed (ʿabara); express! (to a man, ʿabbir)

errors.current: عرفنا = introduce to us! (to a man)
errors.problem: عَرَفْنَا 'we knew, we recognised' is the ordinary reading of this spelling; only the Form II imperative عَرِّفْنَا means 'introduce (to) us'
errors.fix: we knew, we recognised (ʿarafnā); introduce (to) us! (to a man, ʿarrifnā)

errors.problem: عَلِمْتُ 'I knew, I found out' and عَلِمَتْ 'she knew' share the spelling with عَلَّمْتُ 'I taught'; a learner tapping عَلِمْتُ learns a wrong verb
errors.fix: I knew, I found out (ʿalimtu); I taught (ʿallamtu); also you knew / she knew

errors.problem: عَمَلُنَا 'our work' (noun + our) is as common as the verb عَمِلْنَا and is a different part of speech
errors.fix: we worked (ʿamilnā); our work (ʿamalunā)

errors.problem: قُلْتُ 'I said' is by far the commonest reading of this spelling, and قُلْتَ 'you said (to a man)' is also covered; the gloss gives only the feminine 2nd person from one sentence
errors.fix: I said (qultu); you said (qulta to a man, qulti to a woman)

errors.problem: كُتُبُهُ 'his books' shares the spelling; the sibling entry كتبها is glossed 'her books', so the two keys are glossed inconsistently and each one-sidedly
errors.fix: his books (kutubuhu); (he) wrote it (katabahu)

errors.problem: كَتَبَهَا '(he) wrote it (f)' shares the spelling; the verb reading is at least as common as 'her books'
errors.fix: her books (kutubuhā); (he) wrote it (f) (katabahā)

errors.current: ناموا = sleep! go to bed! (to a group)
errors.problem: نَامُوا 'they slept' (past, 3rd plural) is spelled identically to the plural imperative and is the commoner reading in narrative; imperative/past mix-up
errors.fix: they slept (nāmū); sleep!, go to bed! (to a group)

errors.current: نجحت = you succeeded ('will pass', to a man)
errors.problem: نَجَحْتُ 'I passed' and نَجَحَتْ 'she passed' are covered too, and 'will pass' is a leaked translation of one conditional sentence (إذا نجحت), not a meaning of this past-tense form
errors.fix: I passed, I succeeded (najaḥtu); you passed (to a man najaḥta, to a woman najaḥti); she passed (najaḥat)

errors.current: وأقدم = and the oldest (before a noun)

errors.fix: and the oldest (aqdam, before a noun); and I present, I offer (uqaddimu)

errors.problem: وَتَكَلَّمَ 'and he spoke' (past) is spelled identically to the imperative وَتَكَلَّمْ and is the usual reading in narrative; imperative/past mix-up
errors.fix: and (he) spoke (takallama); and speak! (to a man, takallam)

errors.problem: وَجَدْتُهُ 'I found him / it' shares the spelling and is the expected reading next to the sibling entries وجدت = I found and وجدتها = I found it; the gloss gives only wa-jaddatuhu
errors.fix: I found him, I found it (wajadtuhu); and his grandmother (wa-jaddatuhu)

errors.problem: by the same split as وجدته, this key also covers وَجَدَّتُهَا 'and her grandmother'; a learner tapping it in a family sentence gets a verb
errors.fix: I found it, I found her (wajadtuhā); and her grandmother (wa-jaddatuhā)

errors.problem: وَصُوَر 'and pictures, photos' (plural of صورة) shares the spelling and is a basic noun in the course; the gloss gives only the Form II past verb
errors.fix: and pictures, photos (wa-ṣuwar); and (he) photographed (wa-ṣawwara)

errors.problem: يَعْلَمُ '(he) knows' is the commonest reading of this spelling (الله يعلم, لا يعلم); only Form II يُعَلِّمُ means 'teaches'
errors.fix: (he) knows (yaʿlamu); (he) teaches (yuʿallimu)

errors.problem: the key covers the active صَنَعَ '(he) made' and the noun صُنْع 'making, manufacture' as well as the passive صُنِعَ
errors.fix: (he) made (ṣanaʿa); (it) was made (ṣuniʿa); making (ṣunʿ)

errors.problem: ضَيْفًا is singular; it means 'a guest' (object form, كان ضيفًا) and only after 11–99 translates as 'guests'

errors.fix: switch on!, play! (to a man, shaghghil); work, job (shughl)

errors.problem: فَاعِل 'doer; the subject of a verb (grammar term)' shares the spelling and is a grammar term a learner will meet; the gloss gives only the Form III pattern

errors.path: يسمع; يظهر; ينام; يزورنا; يراجع; يرتاح; نسبح; نستمع; نضع; نحمي; نغير; نتزلج; نسهر; نتأخر; نرضي; نركبه; نعطيك; ونسبح; وتحتفلا; يذهبوا; يكونوا
errors.problem: editorial mood notes leaked into dictionary glosses. For يسمع, يظهر, ينام, يزورنا, يراجع, يرتاح, نسبح, نستمع, نضع, نحمي, نغير, نتزلج, نسهر, نتأخر, نرضي, نركبه, نعطيك, ونسبح the unvocalised spelling is identical to the plain present indicative, so '(after an / lam / lan)' is false wherever the word is an ordinary present ('he hears'). Only the plural/dual forms without ن (يذهبوا, يكونوا, وتحتفلا, يأخذا, يركبا, يبحثوا, يقرؤوا) are really marked; for those the note should read 'after an / lan / lam' (any of the three), not just one particle
errors.fix: drop the mood parenthesis on the forms that are spelled like the indicative, e.g. يسمع = he hears; ينام = he sleeps; نسبح = we swim; and on the ن-less forms write 'after an / lan / lam', e.g. يذهبوا = they go (form after an / lan / lam)

errors.path: شربت; صححت; ظننت; غبت; غسلت; فزت; فقدت; قضيت; لاحظت; لبست; مشيت; نسيت; نظفت; نظمت; وجدت; واشتريت; وبقيت; وسمعت; وشربت; وشعرت; وكتبت; وفهمت; ونمت; فأجبت; فتكلمت; فكتبت; قرأتها; فأخذتها; غادرت; قدمت; فاقترحت; فسألته; وأخذت; وتركت; وسألت; وطبخت; ووصلت; وبنيت; غطيت; صنعته; نسيتها; ودفعت; ونسيت; شاهدتك; علمتنا
errors.problem: past-tense verbs ending in ت are glossed with one person only, taken from one sentence. The unvocalised key covers -tu (I), -ta (you, m), -ti (you, f) and -at (she / it f) alike, so e.g. شربت = 'I drank' is wrong when the learner taps شَرِبَتْ 'she drank', قدمت = '(she) presented' is wrong for قَدَّمْتُ 'I presented', ودفعت = 'and you paid (to a man)' is wrong for وَدَفَعْتُ 'and I paid', and صنعته = 'you made it (to a woman)' is wrong for صَنَعْتُهُ 'I made it'
errors.fix: give all persons the spelling covers, e.g. شربت = I drank; you drank (m/f); she drank — قدمت = I / you / she presented ('gave') — ودفعت = and I paid; and you paid — صنعته = I made it; you made it; she made it — نسيتها = I forgot it / left it; you forgot it (f) — ونسيت = and I forgot; and you forgot — شاهدتك = I saw you; she saw you — علمتنا = you taught us; she taught us

errors.path: وتحضر; وتشرب; وتساعد; وتفهم; وتكون; وتغلق; وتكتب; وتعلمني
errors.current: وتحضر = and you bring (to a man)
errors.problem: present-tense verbs with the ت prefix are glossed with one subject only; the spelling covers both 'you (m)' and 'she / it (f)' (and for وتكون, وتغلق, وتكتب also the active 'you / she'), so وتشرب = 'and she drinks' is wrong when the learner taps وَتَشْرَبُ 'and you drink', and وتحضر = 'and you bring' is wrong for 'and she brings / attends'
errors.fix: give both subjects, e.g. وتحضر = and you bring (to a man); and she brings, attends — وتشرب = and she drinks; and you drink (to a man) — وتساعد = and she helps; and you help — وتفهم = and you understand; and she understands — وتكون = and (they, f) are; and you are / she is — وتغلق = and (they, f) are switched off; and you / she close(s) — وتكتب = and (they, f) are written; and you / she write(s)

errors.problem: a possessive or object suffix ك is glossed with a single gender taken from one sentence; the unvocalised key covers both -ka and -ki. summary: Checked all ~1,700 entries of the second half of the auto glossary (س to ي) as dictionary glosses for an unvocalised key. 45 findings: 18 major and 27 minor (five of the minor ones are grouped entries covering about 80 keys). The dominant pattern is one-sided glossing: a key that covers two different words gets only the reading of the sentence it was harvested from (يعلم = teaches but not knows; عرفنا = introduce to us! but not we knew; كتبه = he wrote it vs كتبها = her books; وجدته = and his grandmother vs وجدتها = I found it; ظهرا = back but not at noon; عبر = express! but not across). Second pattern: past verbs in -ت and present verbs in ت- glossed with a single person or gender from one sentence (قلت = you said (to a woman) when I said is the default; ناموا and وتكلم glossed only as imperatives though the past reading is identical). Third: editorial notes leaked into glosses, chiefly '(after an / lam)' on forms whose spelling is also the plain indicative, and 'will pass' on the past نجحت. Noun/verb homographs (وصور, عملنا, وأقدم, وفرنا, وبني) round out the majors. The rest of the chunk is accurate; number phrases, prepositional la-/li- compounds, names and place names were sound.
